entrypoints.summary: The mode-0666 misc device registers challenge_write as its write handler; it consumes an exactly sized packed record containing an address and byte value.

affected_components.role: Resolves a caller-provided virtual address to a page and writes the caller byte through a writable vmap alias.

causal_paths.kind: caller record to physical-page byte store

code_slices.surrounding_context: The handler requires exact input size, excludes addresses below TASK_SIZE_MAX and the vsyscall page, requires a non-executable PTE and valid PFN, and permits only one successful attempt through challenge_once.
code_slices.vulnerable: challenge_write accepts a packed { unsigned long addr; char value; } record, obtains page_for(current->mm, arg.addr), maps that page using vmap(..., PAGE_KERNEL), and writes mapping[arg.addr & ~PAGE_MASK] = arg.value.

capabilities.concept: single-byte modification of a caller-selected qualifying physical page via writable kernel alias

mitigations.concept: authorize a dedicated target object before creating a writable kernel mapping

relation_candidates.dst: single-byte modification of a caller-selected qualifying physical page via writable kernel alias
relation_candidates.rationale: The device exposes challenge_write to mode 0666 callers, accepts an address-and-byte record, resolves the address to a page, aliases it writable, and performs the byte store.
The stored caller-provided byte changes a byte in the resolved physical page, within the handler's stated address, PTE, PFN, and one-use constraints.
relation_candidates.src: single-byte modification of a caller-selected qualifying physical page via writable kernel alias

relation_candidates.dst: authorize a dedicated target object before creating a writable kernel mapping
relation_candidates.rationale: Binding writes to an authorized dedicated object rather than a page resolved from caller input would prevent the observed caller-selected-page alias-and-store path. This is an inferred mitigation, not a supplied patch.
relation_candidates.src: single-byte modification of a caller-selected qualifying physical page via writable kernel alias

impact.affected_asset: Kernel-accessible physical page selected by the supplied address, subject to the code's predicates
impact.attacker_capability: Invoke the device's single-use write with a chosen byte and an address that passes the handler's range, PTE, and PFN checks
impact.security_effect: Integrity modification of one byte in a selected qualifying physical page through kernel-mode mapping

causal_trace.summary: A caller of the world-writable misc device supplies a packed record with an unsigned-long addr and a one-byte value to challenge_write.

The handler verifies record size, excludes user-range and vsyscall addresses, and requires a current-mm PTE resolving to a non-executable valid PFN, but it does not bind the resolved physical page to an authorized challenge-owned object.

After the one-use gate, challenge_write obtains the page for the supplied address, creates a writable PAGE_KERNEL alias with vmap, and stores the caller byte at the supplied page offset through that alias.

A caller able to provide an address satisfying the implemented PTE/PFN predicates can modify one byte of the corresponding selected physical page through a kernel writable mapping; the primitive is limited to one successful use by challenge_once.

failure.operation: Writable PAGE_KERNEL alias creation followed by mapping[arg.addr & ~PAGE_MASK] = arg.value

primary_invariant.statement: A device write handler must only create writable kernel aliases and modify physical pages that belong to an explicitly authorized target object.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The handler derives a page from an attacker-supplied qualifying address in current->mm and aliases it with PAGE_KERNEL, while its checks establish mapping/PTE properties rather than ownership or authorization of the target page.

quality.review_notes: The mechanism is directly localized in inspected module source, including input validation, the single-use gate, vmap(PAGE_KERNEL), and byte store. No execution trace, kernel/initramfs configuration, target-selection exploit, successful post-write outcome, or actual remediation patch is supplied. The Docker configuration exposes SYS_ADMIN and unconfined AppArmor, but it does not establish an exploitation result or privilege escalation.

remediation.invariant_restored: Restrict the write to a dedicated, authorized page or object and reject addresses that merely resolve to otherwise qualifying pages; do not vmap a PFN selected from caller-controlled address input.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The supplied address must be outside the user range, not in the excluded vsyscall page, be mapped in current->mm, resolve to a non-executable PTE, and yield a valid PFN.
data_structure_invariants: The input must exactly match the packed address-and-byte record size.
The target page must satisfy the page_for mapping/PTE/PFN predicates.
Only one attempted successful use is permitted after the atomic exchange.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: Must be at or above TASK_SIZE_MAX, must not have page base equal to VSYSCALL_ADDR, and must resolve through page_for.
numeric_domains.name: addr

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: Caller supplies the byte written at the page offset derived from addr.
numeric_domains.name: value

state_context.state_machine: challenge_once starts at the multi-character constant 'hxp'; atomic_xchg changes it to zero before page lookup, and subsequent write attempts return -EBUSY.
